newsitem.title: USA: Bradys end mixed, players eye Fed's next move.
newsitem.headline: Bradys end mixed, players eye Fed's next move.

text.p: Emerging market debt ended mixed on Friday with some issues outperforming others as players eye the Federal Reserve's next policy move, players said.
"The market was generally quiet. It was very well bid this morning, in particular Brazil, but since has came off with the Dow, and weaker Treasuries," one Brady trader said.
Renewed fears that the Fed will raise short-term interest rates, following a stronger-than-expected U.S. housing report, sent U.S. Treasuries and stocks lower on Friday, traders said.
The Dow Jonee Industrial Average closed off 139 points to 7195 and in the U.S. government market, the 30-year Treasury bond closed off 15/32 at 96-15/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
Despite weakness in other markets, some Brady issues were quoted tighter by about seven basis points, traders said.

"Right now we have a very interesting situation," said another Brady trader. "People are trying to decide, number one what happens next week and number two, given the different scenarios, what the market is going to do."
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet on Tuesday to vote on U.S. monetary policy.

"One scenario is that there's a hike and it's viewed as the last one, in which case eveyone is going to jump in here and buy," the trader said. "The other, there's a hike and it's one of many to come -- in that case the market will get hit hard."
"The third, is there's no hike and in that scenario the market sees a brief rally and then waits for more data to confirm Greenspan's decision," he said.
Results of a preliminary Reuters poll show that U.S. experts are equally divided over whether the Fed will maintain policy as it stands, or hike rates by 25 basis points.
Meanwhile, among Brady issues, Venezuela was particularly well bid as positive sentiment on the credit continued, traders said.

"ING Barings is working on a 10-year global bond. I think that and the fact that Venezuela renewed its IMF standby loan the week before last has pulled people back into the market," said one trader at a large U.S. investment bank.
"A lot of people were cautious when oil prices dropped below $20 a barrel, but I think that overall, people are more interested and they believe more in the credit right now," he said.
Venezuela Flirbs were quoted higher by 1-1/4 at 90-5/8, par bonds were unchanged at 74-3/4.
Turning to Ecuador, a government official said on Friday, Ecuador would issue up to $250 million of bonds in order to make a partial payment of debt owed to the Paris Club.
The official said interest on the bonds would be the prime rate plus one percentage point. The maturities would be between three and five years.
The government of President Fabian Alarcon is currently negotiating with the Paris Club for a restructuring of the $1.2 billion of debt Ecuador has with the organization.
Recently, Ecuador carried out a Brady debt buyback with the proceeds of its first ever $500 million eurobond issue.
Ecuador Pars and Discounts were an 1/8 stronger at 44-3/8 bid and 67-1/2 bid, respectively.
In Mexico, players said a continuation of discount bond buyback rumors kept the paper at tighter levels.
"Mexico Brady debt was tighter by about 20 basis points on continued rumors of a buyback," said one Brady trader.
Mexico Pars gained 3/8 to 74-1/2 bid and discounts ended the trading day up 5/8 at 91 bid.
Among other Latin credits, Argentina Pars were quoted off 1/8 at 66-1/2, Brazil "C" bonds were unchanged at 76 bid.
European Brady debt issues ended Friday's trading session at weaker levels with Bulgaria FLRBs off 1/4 to 50-3/4 bid and Poland Discounts weaker by 3/8 at 98 bid.
Dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh loans ended unchanged at 84-1/2 bid.
